set.body:
Owner: ScalaFIM design/model/fit; general reusable numerical basis generation belongs in Gale if extracted. Consumer: PLS Neuro W3 bd-01M1YVQ44TVRBAY11F30K7BTA1 under selective-estimation epic bd-01M1ZAMMWZCNK5C9CXCVZ1WYTS.

Adopted consumer requirement: explicit cutoff-period drift controls with native design review and the same joint model in execution. The current public BaselineBasis API exposes Constant/Poly/Bs/Ns and rejects parse("dct"); ModelBuildSpec has no cutoff field. A compiled Java public-API probe against the admitted frozen ScalaFIM candidate confirms that bounded gap. Source: /private/tmp/DctDriftCapabilityProbe.java; receipt: /private/tmp/plsneuro-dct-capability/receipt.json. Admitted provider base fd992a0c85001eb50ba2e78d29c497693ca494dc, patch 2d52a48eddbd422b5751dc94720fe2eb9dd0fc11267b0d60494bcdc61ca45b75. Native checkout has since advanced; inspect exact source before implementation/adoption.

Implement a typed cutoff-period DCT drift model that preserves per-run original acquisition positions, permits different basis counts for different run lengths/TRs, treats intercept policy explicitly, reports exact column counts/cutoff/units and preserves meaningful schema identity. Keep default behavior unchanged; no universal cutoff or filter default. Bound invalid/non-finite periods, excessive basis counts and unsupported grids explicitly. Censoring selects original rows instead of rebuilding a compressed time grid. Define the cutoff endpoint convention with a cited primary reference and an independent fixture.

Retain one scientific fitting path: drift columns enter the native nuisance/design model so the selected OLS operator adjusts data and design consistently without an extra full-BOLD preprocessing pass. Verify equivalence to independent residualization using the same retained rows. Do not treat temporal filtering and GLS whitening as interchangeable or assume they commute. Duplicate/conflicting supplied drift regressors require an explicit, inspectable policy and normal rank/estimability diagnostics.

Resolve reusable basis ownership before coding a second DCT kernel: latent/DctBasis.scala already contains a portable DCT-II basis, while design deliberately does not depend on latent. Avoid an upward design-to-latent dependency and duplicate kernels. If general basis generation moves to Gale, create its native implementation issue and keep a foreign-ID provenance link here rather than a cross-store dependency edge; requalify the existing latent consumer separately.

Acceptance: independent scalar/reference DCT entries and cutoff counts; orthogonality/constant handling; mixed TR/length, short/empty-basis and invalid-period cases; original scan/run identity under censoring; unchanged legacy baselines; structural rank/alias diagnostics; equality of adjusted task estimates versus an independent full-model/residualization oracle; targeted full module/platform JVM+Scala.js gates and direct consumer checks. Documentation must explain the exact period convention and scientific effect. PLS Neuro owns editor/persistence/native visual integration and exact candidate adoption.

Primary references consulted: https://github.com/spm/spm/blob/main/spm_filter.m (cutoff column selection and residual projection) and https://github.com/spm/spm/blob/main/spm_dctmtx.m (normalized DCT-II convention). These inform an explicit new native contract, not an unqualified SPM pipeline-equivalence claim.
set.title: Support cutoff-period DCT drift in native first-level design and fitting
